{{Vanilla|Redstone Ore}}
{{Infobox auto}}
A '''fossil''' is an [[Ores|ore]] that drops {{MCW|Bone|bones}}. It is the vanilla {{MCW|Redstone Ore|redstone ore}}, renamed and given new drops and generation in {{Version|1.12.8-beta}}; before that, the same block was the '''sulfurous quartz deposit''', which dropped [[Sulfur Chunk|sulfur]] and [[quartz]]. Fossils give a source of bones that doesn't depend on killing skeletons, which the release notes sum up as "Peaceful bones".<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.8-beta|quote=Fossil "Ore" can now be found (Peaceful bones!)}}</ref> The deepslate variant of the same ore is still the [[Sulfur Deposit|sulfur deposit]].

== Obtaining ==
=== Natural generation ===
Fossils generate in every Overworld biome in veins of up to 8 blocks, 4 attempts per chunk, between y=16 and y=56, most often around y=36.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/worldgen/placed_feature/ore_redstone.json}}</ref> This replaces the vanilla redstone placement (4 attempts per chunk spread evenly from the world bottom to y=15). The vein uses the vanilla redstone ore feature, which places fossils in stone, granite, diorite, andesite and tuff, and a [[Sulfur Deposit|sulfur deposit]] wherever it meets deepslate. The vanilla lower redstone veins, deep in the deepslate layer, are unchanged and only place sulfur deposits.

=== Breaking ===
Mined with a [[Copper Pickaxe|copper pickaxe]] or better (a [[Wooden Pickaxe|wooden pickaxe]] or [[Copper Dolabra|copper dolabra]] gets nothing; see [[Tools#Mining levels]]), it drops 2–5 bones. Fortune and [[Electrum equipment|electrum]] tools each add to the count with the usual ore bonus. Silk Touch drops the block itself.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/redstone_ore.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/block/non_mineable/wood.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/copper_dolabra.json}}</ref>

== Usage ==
Bones from fossils are ordinary bones, used for bone meal and anything else that takes a bone.
